title: Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar Reaffirms Commitment to Inclusive Development and Empowerment of Marginalised Communities
subtitle:
NAMASTE, SEED and PM-AJAY Schemes Strengthen Safety, Livelihoods, Education and Opportunities for Vulnerable Communities
Dr Virendra Kumar Conducts Exhaustive Interaction Session With The Beneficiaries Of The SEED, NAMASTE & PM-AJAY Schemes; Also Administer ‘Pledge Against Drug Abuse’
body_text:
Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar today reaffirmed the Central Government's commitment towards ensuring that no citizen or community is left behind in the country's development journey. He emphasised that the true meaning of social justice lies in ensuring that the benefits of development reach those at the margins and that every citizen receives equal opportunities, dignity and respect.
Addressing the beneficiaries of SEED, NAMASTE and PM-AJAY schemes of the Ministry at a function at Dr Ambedkar International Centre in National Capital, Dr Kumar highlighted the continued efforts of the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment towards the empowerment of disadvantaged, vulnerable and needy sections of society.
Secretary, Shri Sudhansh Pant, Additional Secretary Smt Mona A Khandar, Joint Secretary Dr Sandeep R Rathod, MD, NSKFDC Shri Prabhat Kumar Singh, Other Senior Officers and officials of the Ministry were present on the occasion.
Dr Kumar said that through initiatives such as SEED, NAMASTE and PM-AJAY, the Government is working not merely to provide assistance but also to create sustainable opportunities in education, livelihood, social security and dignified living.
The Minister said that under the NAMASTE scheme , the Government is working towards ensuring the safety, dignity and sustainable livelihood of sanitation workers while promoting safe and mechanised sanitation practices. He highlighted that the measures including profiling of sewer and septic tank workers, provision of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits, health insurance, safety training and Emergency Sanitation Response Units are being undertaken. He added that the Scheme also cover waste pickers with the objective of integrating them into the formal solid waste management system while ensuring safer and dignified livelihood opportunities.
The Minister said that the Government is also committed to the rehabilitation of persons engaged in manual scavenging and elimination of hazardous manual cleaning. The Minister stressed that every sanitation worker deserves a safe workplace, social security and a dignified life.
The Union Minister flagged the commitment of the Government to work towards the social and economic empowerment of Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic (DNT, NT and SNT) communities adding that the SEED (Scheme for Economic Empowerment of DNTs) Scheme is one of the landmark initiatives of the Ministry. He added that the initiative seeks to go beyond financial assistance by creating opportunities for sustainable livelihoods, skill development, self-reliance and a dignified life.
Dr Kumar said that special emphasis is being placed on the empowerment of women from DNT communities wherein a broader objective of the SEED initiative is to create an empowered woman, an empowered family, an empowered community and, ultimately, an Atmanirbhar Bharat.
Dr Kumar highlighted the importance of Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) which is another key initiative aimed at the social, economic and educational empowerment of Scheduled Caste communities. He said the Scheme focuses on reducing poverty and expanding employment and livelihood opportunities, developing infrastructure in Scheduled Caste-majority areas, and increasing the participation of Scheduled Caste students in school and higher education.
The Minister also highlighted the launch of the PM-AJAY mobile application and portal in May 2026 , which is aimed at moving scheme implementation from paper-based processes towards real-time digital workflows, thereby strengthening monitoring, transparency and accountability.
On the occasion, the Union Minister administered ‘Pledge Against Drug Abuse’ in which all the participants pledged to work against the drug abuse and welfare and rehabilitation of the victims of substance abuse, to make India a drug dree country.
Dr Virendra Kumar had an exhaustive interaction session with the beneficiaries of the SEED, NAMASTE & PM-AJAY Schemes. The Minister emphasised that the Government's objective extends beyond the implementation of welfare schemes to expanding opportunities and enabling communities to become self-reliant. He said that empowered women, families and communities constitute the strong foundation of a self-reliant and developed India.
On the eve of Independence Day celebration , the Minister extended greetings to all beneficiaries and stakeholders associated with these initiatives and acknowledged their hard work, talent and confidence as important strengths of the nation.
The Minister called for collective efforts to build an India where every citizen has equal opportunities and every community can contribute to nation-building to its full potential. He reiterated the Government's resolve that no person should be left behind in the journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047 , and that every citizen should have access to dignity and equal opportunity.

enrichment.summary: Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar addressed beneficiaries of the NAMASTE, SEED and PM-AJAY schemes at Dr Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi, reaffirming the government's commitment to inclusive development of sanitation workers, Denotified/Nomadic/Semi-Nomadic communities and Scheduled Castes. He highlighted scheme features such as PPE kits, health insurance and profiling of sanitation workers under NAMASTE, skill development and women's empowerment under SEED, and the May 2026 launch of the PM-AJAY mobile app/portal for digital monitoring. He also administered a 'Pledge Against Drug Abuse' and interacted with scheme beneficiaries ahead of Independence Day.
enrichment.context:
NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem) is a joint scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs aimed at eliminating hazardous manual scavenging, ensuring safety and dignity for sanitation and sewer workers, and integrating waste pickers into formal solid waste management. SEED (Scheme for Economic Empowerment of DNTs) targets Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes—communities historically stigmatized under the colonial-era Criminal Tribes Act and still lacking formal ST/SC/OBC-equivalent recognition in many states—by providing livelihood support, education, health insurance and legal aid. PM-AJAY (Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana), launched by merging earlier schemes like PMAGY, Adarsh Gram Yojana and SC sub-plan components, focuses on poverty reduction, infrastructure development in SC-majority villages ('Adarsh Grams'), and higher education support for SC students via hostels and grants-in-aid.

This release is essentially a ceremonial/interactive event around Independence Day, reiterating existing scheme objectives rather than announcing new policy, funding, or targets. The only concrete new element is the mention of the PM-AJAY mobile app/portal launched in May 2026 for digital monitoring—useful for tracking governance-technology convergence in welfare delivery, a recurring UPSC theme.

prelims_questions.question: The NAMASTE scheme is jointly implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and which other ministry?
options: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
prelims_questions.explanation: NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem) is jointly run by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to ensure safety and dignity for sanitation workers.

prelims_questions.question: The SEED scheme is aimed at the economic empowerment of which category of communities?
prelims_questions.explanation: SEED (Scheme for Economic Empowerment of DNTs) targets Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic communities, providing livelihood, skill development and welfare support.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the challenges faced by manual scavengers and sanitation workers in India despite legal prohibitions, and evaluate the effectiveness of schemes like NAMASTE in addressing these challenges.

Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes remain among the most marginalised groups in India due to historical stigmatisation. Examine the objectives of the SEED scheme and suggest measures for their effective social and economic integration.

study_notes.reason: The release is largely ceremonial, but it usefully consolidates factual details of three distinct schemes (NAMASTE, SEED, PM-AJAY) whose names, target groups and implementing features are classic prelims fodder; analytical content is thin and mostly reiterates known objectives.

prelims.point: NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem) is a joint scheme of Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs for sanitation/sewer workers and waste pickers.
prelims.why_important: The dual-ministry ownership and target group (sanitation workers, waste pickers) is a common point of confusion UPSC tests via statement-based questions.

prelims.point: SEED (Scheme for Economic Empowerment of DNTs) targets Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNT/NT/SNT), historically linked to the colonial Criminal Tribes Act.
prelims.why_important: DNT/NT/SNT communities lack formal SC/ST/OBC-equivalent status in many states, making this a frequently tested distinction in social justice topics.

prelims.point: PM-AJAY (Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana) was formed by merging earlier schemes (PMAGY, Adarsh Gram Yojana, SC sub-plan components) and focuses on SC-majority village development ('Adarsh Grams') and higher education support.
prelims.why_important: Knowing the schemes merged into PM-AJAY helps distinguish it from other SC welfare schemes in objective questions.

prelims.point: NAMASTE includes profiling of sewer/septic tank workers, PPE kits, health insurance, safety training and Emergency Sanitation Response Units.
prelims.why_important: Specific scheme components are typical targets for 'which of the following are features of the scheme' questions.

prelims.point: PM-AJAY mobile application/portal for digital, real-time monitoring was announced for launch in May 2026.
prelims.why_important: Scheme-specific digital governance tools and their launch timelines are testable factual details.

mains.point: Digitisation of welfare scheme monitoring (PM-AJAY portal) reflects a governance shift from paper-based to real-time accountability systems, relevant to debates on last-mile delivery and transparency in SC welfare implementation.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for answers on how technology can strengthen implementation and accountability in social sector schemes, and the persistent gap between digital tools and ground-level delivery.

mains.point: SEED scheme's focus on DNT/NT/SNT communities highlights the continuing lack of constitutional/legal recognition for these groups despite decades since decriminalisation of the Criminal Tribes Act.
mains.theme: Social justice for unrecognised marginalised groups
mains.analytical_use: Can be used in questions on gaps in India's reservation/welfare framework for communities not covered under SC/ST/OBC categories.
